# Design brief

## Owner's direction (standing rules for every project)

Avoid the generic "AI slop" look. Make it distinctive and designed for this context.

- **Typography:** beautiful, unusual fonts. Not Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts or Space Grotesk. An Arabic pairing with real character. All fonts self-hosted.
- **Colour and theme:** one committed palette held in CSS variables. Dominant colours with sharp accents, not timid even palettes. No purple gradients on white. Inspiration can come from IDE themes and cultural aesthetics. A real dark mode.
- **Motion:** CSS-first. One well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (`animation-delay`) instead of scattered micro-interactions.
- **Backgrounds:** atmosphere and depth. Layer gradients, use geometric patterns and effects that fit the context, not flat solid colours.
- **Layout:** no predictable, cookie-cutter component patterns.

## This project's concept

Working concept: **"… meets …"** (one line that ties the episode's subject to a visual world; e.g. "the lab notebook meets the Hejaz", "Najdi adobe and ink").

- **Why it fits the episode:** …
- **Palette:** base, text, accent (and what the accent is reserved for, e.g. timestamps), dark-mode version.
- **Type:** display, body, mono/labels; Arabic display and body.
- **Motif:** a pattern or texture, where it appears and how strong.
- **Signature motion:** what happens on page load.
- **Interactive pieces:** see the outline.
